title: Reversible cross-IDE Rulesync context pilot
objective: A reversible Rulesync-generated context set for Jobby development only, with static gates before any model sessions and no product/UI deployment.

requirements.statement: Canonical .rulesync source owns generation. Native Cursor/Codex/Claude discovery owns loading. No runtime context manager, MCP product changes, global config, or production dependencies.
Generation is reproducible from a pinned public CLI. Dry-run/check produce no unauthorized outputs. Content hashes and a duplicate-identity inventory exist.

Static tests fail closed on missing references, cycles, and path escapes, and cover ordinary vs forced updater pruning plus rollback hash restoration. An ordinary (non-force) prune never removes a tracked fork-only skill; forcing a prune that removes one produces a deletion report naming each removed path.
No push, merge, or adoption before the listed gates pass. The work stays on an isolated worktree from the named base commit.

The >=50% repository instruction payload reduction is measured in tokens, per client (Cursor/Codex/Claude counted separately), plus a combined total reported alongside — never bytes, never a single blended number in place of the per-client figures. Only files the client actually loads as repository instructions count toward the baseline or the candidate.

Full-task completion quality/usage is out of scope for this pilot and is recorded as explicitly unmeasured, not inferred from the payload-reduction figures. A separate future evaluation may measure it; this pilot's acceptance never depends on it.

The Jobby-specific QA skill is namespaced distinctly from any generic QA skill (e.g. `jobby/qa-manual-automation`), so rulesync generation never has to pick a winner between them. If generation ever produces two skills that would resolve to the same identity, that is a fail-closed error, not a silent overwrite.

A source overlay applies as a safe merge into its target file. If a safe merge cannot be computed (conflicting regions, unrecognized target structure), generation fails closed rather than silently replacing the whole file. Whole-file replacement is available only behind an explicit per-overlay opt-in.

origin.reference: Owner decision, 2026-09-25 — resolves the overlay-replacement risk named in intake

requirements.statement: Codex's topic-based rule grouping survives generation via headings or metadata in the generated output, not a flattened list. A round-trip test proves no grouping is lost between the canonical source and the generated Codex output.

origin.reference: Owner decision, 2026-09-25 — resolves the Codex topic-flattening risk named in intake

requirements.statement: Token counting is deterministic and offline: js-tiktoken@1.0.21 (pinned devDependency, lockfile-verified), o200k_base encoding, no network call and no model inference in the loop. Per client, the counted set is a SPECIFIED FILE-SET PROXY, not a verified claim of what the client always loads at runtime — Claude Code: CLAUDE.md plus every file it @-imports, recursively; Cursor: .cursorrules if present plus every .cursor/rules/*.mdc file whose frontmatter sets alwaysApply: true; Codex: AGENTS.md plus CODEX.md if present. Conditionally-loaded content (glob/description-gated Cursor rules, on-demand Claude skills) is excluded from both baseline and candidate by the same specified rule. Files are concatenated in the client's own load order with a single newline between files, then tokenized as one string; the count is encoding.encode(text).length. Known inaccuracies against real client behavior, not yet resolved by session evidence: official Codex guidance selects at most one instruction file per directory rather than always loading both AGENTS.md and CODEX.md together; Claude Code rules with no `paths`/glob restriction may load without a CLAUDE.md @-import, so the true load set for the generated .claude/rules/*.md files (which currently carry `paths`) depends on observed client behavior, not this algorithm. Report every number from this method as 'specified file-set proxy', never as measured session usage, and never as a billable/cached model-token cost, until the 24-session matrix (REQ-RS-006's deferred full-task usage) confirms or corrects it per client.

origin.reference: Owner decision, 2026-09-25 — reproducible counting method; corrected 2026-09-25 against observed rulesync/Codex/Claude Code loading behavior (see https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory)

requirements.statement: The pass/fail gate is evaluated per client: for each of Cursor, Codex, and Claude independently, reduction_pct = (baseline_tokens - candidate_tokens) / baseline_tokens must be >= 0.50. All three must individually clear the threshold; one client's larger reduction never offsets another's shortfall. The combined total across all three clients is computed and reported for visibility only and is never itself the pass condition. A client whose baseline_tokens is 0 is reported as not_applicable and excluded from the gate rather than causing a divide-by-zero or an automatic pass.

scenarios.title: Authorized generation only
given: The pinned Rulesync CLI and the canonical .rulesync source are present.
then: Outputs are limited to the declared ownership set.
No unauthorized files are written.

scenarios.title: Missing references and cycles fail closed
given: A source overlay is missing a required reference or contains a cycle or escape.
then: The check fails.
Adoption stays blocked.

scenarios.title: Ordinary updater prune keeps fork-only skills
given: Tracked fork-only skills sit outside updater-owned paths.
then: Those skills remain.
A forced prune is a separate, explicit case.

scenarios.title: Forced prune of fork-only skills produces a deletion report
given: Tracked fork-only skills sit outside updater-owned paths.
scenarios.when: A forced (--force) updater prune removes one or more of them.
then: A deletion report lists each removed path by name.
Nothing is removed silently.

scenarios.title: Rollback restores hashes
given: A prior generation snapshot and its content hashes exist.
then: Restored files match the prior hashes.

scenarios.title: Isolation before adoption
scenarios.when: Someone would push, merge, or adopt the candidate.
then: Adoption stays blocked.
The original checkout is unchanged.

scenarios.title: Per-client token reduction reported separately from the combined total
given: A baseline and a candidate instruction set exist for Cursor, Codex, and Claude.
then: Each client's token reduction is reported individually.
A combined total is reported alongside, never in place of the per-client figures.
Files excluded from the specified file-set proxy (REQ-RS-010) are excluded from both baseline and candidate counts.
The report is labeled a specified file-set proxy, never claimed as measured session usage or a verified native-loading count, until session evidence (REQ-RS-006) confirms it per client.

scenarios.title: Full-task usage stays explicitly unmeasured
then: Full-task completion quality is marked unmeasured, not inferred from token reduction.
Pilot acceptance does not depend on a full-task usage figure.

scenarios.title: Jobby QA skill identity never collides with a generic QA skill
given: Both a generic QA skill and the Jobby-specific QA skill are present as generation inputs.
then: The Jobby skill is emitted under its namespaced identity (e.g. jobby/qa-manual-automation).
If any two generated skills would still resolve to the same identity, generation fails closed instead of picking a winner.

scenarios.title: Overlay merge failure fails closed instead of replacing the file
given: A source overlay's target region cannot be safely merged (conflict or unrecognized structure).
scenarios.when: Generation runs without an explicit whole-file-replacement opt-in for that overlay.
then: Generation fails closed.
The target file is not replaced wholesale.

scenarios.title: Codex topic grouping survives a round trip
given: The canonical source defines Codex rules grouped by topic.
scenarios.when: Generation produces the Codex output and the round-trip test runs.
then: Every topic grouping in the source is identifiable in the generated output via headings or metadata.
No topic's rules are flattened into an unlabeled list.

scenarios.title: Token count is deterministic across repeated runs
given: The same file set and the same pinned js-tiktoken version.
scenarios.when: The counting script runs twice, offline, with no changes to the files in between.
then: Both runs produce byte-identical token counts.
No network call is made.

scenarios.title: Per-client gate is independent; combined total cannot rescue a failing client
given: Two clients individually clear 50% reduction and one client is at 30%, but the combined total across all three is above 50%.
then: The gate reports FAIL, because the 30% client did not individually clear the threshold.
The combined total is shown in the report but does not change the PASS/FAIL outcome.
